target.title: fix(auth): prioritize explicit models.json apiKey over store profiles
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a bug where an explicit `apiKey` configured directly inside the user's `models.json` file is ignored if there are any credential profiles saved in the global profile store (e.g. from onboarding or other agents). This happened because `resolveApiKeyForProvider` failed to check and return the resolved `literal` kind binding from `resolveProviderEntryApiKeyBinding`, falling through to scan the global profile store instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added an immediate handler check inside `resolveApiKeyForProvider` in `src/agents/model-auth.ts` to check if the resolved `providerEntryBinding` is of kind `literal` and return it immediately, bypassing the profile store scan.

## User Impact

Allows users to successfully configure and override provider API keys via `models.json` even if they have active saved profile credentials in their global configuration store.

## Evidence

Passed unit tests on branch `fix/1.1-model-auth-literal-apikey-priority` in `src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts`:
```
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts (72 tests) 174ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  72 passed (72)
```

### Real Behavior Proof

Checked that running the model auth resolver prioritized the literal key from config over the database profile:
```
// Models config:
providers: { "demo-local": { apiKey: "explicit-literal-key" } }

// Store profiles:
"demo-local:default" with key "profile-key-to-ignore"

// Resulting resolved credentials:
{
  apiKey: "explicit-literal-key",
  source: "models.json",
  mode: "api-key"
}
```
